transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I'm mainly here because my sleep has just gotten so unreliable lately. Even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there... replaying sales forecasts and dealing with team issues in my head. And then, if I do manage to fall asleep, I usually end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again after that.
How long have you been experiencing these sleep problems? Has this been going on for weeks, months, or longer?

It's definitely been longer than a few weeks. Um, I'd say this has really been building up since we had a big reorganization in the sales division. That was about thirteen months ago. So, yeah, it's been going on for a little over a year now.
Besides the sleep problems, how has your mood been over this past year? Have you been feeling sad, down, or just not yourself?

Um, I wouldn't really say I've been feeling sad or down. It's not like that. I just... I feel stressed out and wound up most of the time, you know? Like my brain won't stop. But as far as feeling depressed or crying or anything like that, no, I haven't really had that happen. I'm mostly just always on edge.

When you say your brain won't stop, what kinds of things are you typically worrying about? Is it mainly work-related, or do you find yourself worrying about other areas of your life too—like your health, finances, relationships, or things in general?

It's a mix, honestly. Work is a big part of it, but it definitely spills over into other things. Most days, my mind just jumps from one thing to the next. I'll start out worrying about whether we'll hit our launch numbers, and then I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is unhappy and about to quit. 

But then it shifts to other stuff, like the mortgage, or back to a client renewal. It just keeps going. It basically feels like every small delay or hiccup could turn into something major, and I just can't stop playing it all out in my head.

On days when work is going smoothly and there are no obvious problems, are you still able to worry less and feel more relaxed, or does the worry and tension continue pretty much regardless of what's actually happening?

Even when things are going fine, it doesn't really stop. Like, I can tell myself, "Brenda, you've done the plan, just let it go." But... I don't know, maybe five minutes later I'm right back in another loop. It's like I check one concern off my list, and three more just pop up to take its place. So, yeah, it pretty much continues no matter what's actually happening at work.
Besides the racing thoughts and sleep problems, have you noticed any physical symptoms when you're feeling wound up and stressed—like muscle tension, feeling restless or jittery, or trembling?

Yeah, I definitely get that. I feel wound up almost all the time. It's like... even when I'm just at home eating dinner, my body feels like I'm sitting in a high-pressure pipeline review. And my shoulders, they're just constantly tight. No matter how much I try to relax or stretch them out, they just stay tense. I guess I just always feel restless, like I can't fully settle down.

How has all of this stress and worry affected your ability to do your job or perform well at work? Has it impacted your relationships with family or friends, or your ability to enjoy things you normally would?

Yeah, it's definitely starting to affect both my work and my home life. At work, I spend so much time second-guessing my decisions lately... it just makes things like my pipeline reviews run really tense. I'm just overthinking everything instead of just leading the meeting. 

And then, by the time I actually get home, I'm just so drained from it all. I end up being pretty reactive over small things, and I'm just... I'm not fully present with my husband. I just don't have the mental energy left to really engage or enjoy the evening with him.

Have you ever had sudden episodes where you felt a wave of intense fear or panic come over you, even when there wasn't an obvious threat or trigger? And if so, did those episodes come with physical symptoms like a racing heart, chest tightness, or feeling like you couldn't breathe?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I feel stressed and tense all the time, but I wouldn't say I've ever had a sudden wave of panic out of nowhere. My heart doesn't race like that, and I don't get chest tightness or feel like I can't breathe. It's more just a constant, low-level hum of worry rather than a sudden attack.

You mentioned the reorganization happened about thirteen months ago and the sleep problems started around then. But thinking back even further—before that reorganization—would you say you were generally a worrier? Or did this pattern of constant worry and tension really start after the reorganization?

I wouldn't say I was a constant worrier before that. I mean, I had normal stress, but nothing like this. This whole thing... the constant tension and the worry, it really has just been building since that sales division reorganization. So yeah, it's been about thirteen months of this.

You mentioned that even when work is going smoothly, the worry continues. But let me ask more specifically: if you were to take a week-long vacation away from work and all your usual responsibilities, do you think the constant worry and tension would ease up significantly, or would it pretty much stay the same?

I'm honestly not sure. I haven't taken a real vacation since all of this started, so I don't know for certain. I'd like to think it would ease up if I were away from the office for a week, but... given how I feel even on the weekends or when things are actually going fine at work, I kind of suspect the worry would just follow me there. I don't really know, though.

When you think about the reorganization that happened thirteen months ago—has that situation actually improved or stabilized at work since then, or is the workplace situation still as chaotic and uncertain as it was right after the reorganization?

I suppose it has stabilized, technically. I mean, the new structure has been in place for a while now, so the actual day-to-day changes are over. But... I don't know, it still feels just as uncertain to me. Even when things are running normally on paper, I'm just constantly waiting for the next big problem to hit or for things to get upended again. So the workplace itself is probably fine now, but my mind still feels like it's right in the middle of all that chaos.
